title: Relative planar operation extension through cocone-preserving restriction
statement:
Use the quasicategory, coherent-functor and mapping-space conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the unital planar operation systems of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. Let $j:C\to T$ be a coherent functor, where $T$ admits all small colimits, and let $R$ be a collection of specified cocones in $C$ that $j$ sends to colimiting cocones. For every finite $r\geq0$ and every cocomplete target $Z$, assume restriction induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(T^r,Z)\xrightarrow{(j^r)^*}\operatorname{Fun}_R(C^r,Z),$$
where the right side is the full coherent category of functors sending each relation in $R$ to a colimiting cocone in every variable. Let $(t_r)_{r\geq0}$ be a unital planar operation system on $C$, and let separately cocontinuous operations $M_r:T^r\to T$ be equipped with coherent equivalences $\theta_r:M_rj^r\simeq jt_r$, with the specified unary identity and nullary unit comparisons. Then the substitution equivalences and every tree-indexed higher compatibility simplex of $(t_r)$ lift uniquely up to a contractible space to substitution equivalences and all tree-indexed higher compatibility simplices for $(M_r)$, making $\theta=(\theta_r)$ a morphism of unital planar operation systems. All coherences are stated on reduced external input lists before pullback along coordinate projections; nullary vertices are included.

source.place: Higher Algebra §§4.1.2-4.1.3 and §4.8.1; relative finite-variable extension extracted from the proof of Proposition 4.8.1.3. Online source, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Fix a finite planar rooted tree with ordered external input list of length $r$. Each vertex is one of the operations $M_s$, and every external variable occurs in exactly one vertex subtree. Therefore the composite functor $T^r\to T$ associated to the tree is separately cocontinuous: in a variable occurring at a given vertex, the corresponding inner operation preserves the relevant colimits and the outer operations preserve colimits in that input after the other inputs are fixed; composing the comparison maps gives preservation of the colimit. The same argument applies to all contractions and graftings, and to trees with nullary vertices. This is the elementary closure of separate cocontinuity under substitution on reduced input lists.

source.place: Higher Algebra §4.1.2, planar substitution operations and reduced external input lists

proof.text: For every $N\geq0$ let $E_N=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(T^N,T)$ and $F_N=\operatorname{Fun}_R(C^N,T)$, full subcategories of the functor quasicategories $\operatorname{Fun}(T^N,T)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(C^N,T)$, hence quasicategories. By the hypothesis with $Z=T$, restriction $G_N=(j^N)^*:E_N\to F_N$ is a functor equivalence. By step 1 every tree composite of the $M_s$ with $N$ external inputs lies in $E_N$. Postcomposition with $j$ is a simplicial map $\operatorname{Fun}(C^N,C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(C^N,T)$, so it carries every substitution equivalence and every tree-indexed higher simplex of $(t_s)$ with $N$ external inputs to a simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(C^N,T)$. Its vertices $j\circ(\text{tree composite of the }t_s)$ lie in $F_N$: whiskering the $\theta_s$ along the tree (innermost vertices first) gives an equivalence edge $\varepsilon_\Gamma$ from $G_N(\text{tree composite of the }M_s)$ to $j\circ(\text{tree composite of the }t_s)$, and $F_N$ is closed under equivalence because a cocone equivalent to a colimiting cocone is colimiting. Since $F_N$ is a full subcategory, the whole $j$-image of the coherence data of $(t_s)$ lies in $F_N$. For the corolla $\Gamma$ with $N$ inputs, $\varepsilon_\Gamma=\theta_N$; for $N=0$ the corolla is the nullary unit and $\varepsilon=\theta_0$.

source.place: Higher Algebra §4.8.1, relative extension along an equivalence of finite-variable functor categories

proof.text: Lifting lemma. Let $G:E\to F$ be a functor equivalence of quasicategories, $K\subseteq L$ a simplicial subset of a finite simplicial set, $b:K\to E$, $\sigma:L\to F$, and $\varepsilon$ an equivalence edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,F)$ from $Gb$ to $\sigma|_K$. Claim: there are $\tau:L\to E$ with $\tau|_K=b$ and an equivalence edge $\eta$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(L,F)$ from $G\tau$ to $\sigma$ with $\eta|_K=\varepsilon$, and the space of such pairs is contractible. Proof. Postcomposition with $G$, with its quasi-inverse and with the two natural equivalences, makes $\operatorname{Fun}(L,G)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,G)$ functor equivalences (simplicial maps preserve the inverse-triangle witnesses). Restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(L,F)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,F)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ are isofibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Put $P=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,F)}\operatorname{Fun}(L,F)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-equivalence] $P$ is a quasicategory and $P\to\operatorname{Fun}(L,F)$ is a functor equivalence; its composite with the comparison $c:\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)\to P$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(L,G)$, so by [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](2) and two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] $c$ is a functor equivalence. Both $\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)$ and $P$ are isofibred over $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ ($P$ as a pullback of an isofibration), so [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-base-change] at the vertex $b$ gives a functor equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}_b(L,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{Gb}(L,F)$ between the fibres, the categories of maps restricting to $b$, resp. $Gb$, with all simplices constant on $K$. Lifting the inverse of $\varepsilon$ with source $\sigma$ along the isofibration $\operatorname{Fun}(L,F)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,F)$ gives $\sigma'$ with $\sigma'|_K=Gb$ and an equivalence $\sigma'\simeq\sigma$ restricting to $\varepsilon$. Essential surjectivity of the fibre equivalence gives $\tau$ with an equivalence $G\tau\simeq\sigma'$ constant on $K$; to compose, fill the inner horn formed by these two edges by a $2$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(L,F)$ lying over the degenerate $2$-simplex on $\varepsilon$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,F)$ (restriction is an inner fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]); its long edge is $\eta$, and $\eta|_K=\varepsilon$ exactly. ($P$ is isofibred over $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ because lifting properties are stable under pullback.) The pairs $(\tau,\eta)$ form the homotopy fibre over $\sigma'$ of the map of cores of a functor equivalence, which is contractible.

source.place: Higher Algebra §4.8.1, lifting structured data through restriction equivalences; the lifting lemma is assembled by the agent from the cited quasicategory nodes

proof.text: Inductive claim $(I_n)$: every coherence datum of $(t_s)$ of simplicial dimension $\leq n$ (vertices are tree composites; edges are substitution, contraction, grafting and unary-identity equivalences and their inverses; higher simplices are the tree-indexed compatibilities, including those comparing a grafted tree's coherence with the substitution of the coherences of its pieces) with $N$ external inputs has a lift $\tau:\Delta^m\to E_N$ ($m\leq n$) of the same shape for $(M_s)$, with an equivalence $\eta_\tau:G_N\tau\simeq j\circ(\text{datum})$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^m,F_N)$; lifts are compatible with faces and degeneracies, and $\eta$ restricts on each face to the $\eta$ of that face. Base $n=0$: the lift of a tree composite is the composite of the $M_s$ and $\eta=\varepsilon_\Gamma$ from step 2. Step $n-1\to n$: for a datum $\sigma$ of dimension $n$ its faces have lifts by $(I_{n-1})$ which agree on common faces, hence glue to $b:\partial\Delta^n\to E_N$, and their $\eta$ glue to an equivalence $\varepsilon$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^n,F_N)$ from $G_Nb$ to $(j\circ\sigma)|_{\partial\Delta^n}$. Apply step 3 with $G=G_N$, $K=\partial\Delta^n\subseteq L=\Delta^n$: a filler $\tau$ with $\eta_\tau$ restricting to $\varepsilon$ exists, with contractible space of choices. The lifts in dimension $n$ are chosen independently given dimension $<n$, so the space of all lifts is the limit of a tower of maps with contractible fibres, hence contractible. Restrictions of the lifted data are therefore identified with the prescribed data of $(t_s)$ by the coherent equivalences $\eta$, not equal to them; for edges ($n=1$) this is lifting the substitution equivalences, their inverses and the unary identity comparison.

source.place: Higher Algebra §4.1.3, homotopy-coherent tree compatibilities; §4.8.1, relative lifting

proof.text: For $r=0$ both sides of the hypothesis are $\operatorname{Fun}(*,T)=T$ and $G_0$ is the identity, so the nullary unit $M_0$ with $\theta_0$ and all coherences of trees with no external input are handled by the same induction with $F_0=T$; no unused variable is introduced, and nullary vertices inside larger trees were included in steps 1-4. The equivalences $\eta$ of step 4, with the $\theta_r$ on corollas, are exactly coherent equivalences $j\circ(\text{coherence of }t)\simeq(\text{coherence of }M)\circ j^N$ compatible with all planar substitution, unit and higher tree simplices, i.e. $\theta$ is a morphism of unital planar operation systems in the sense of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. All of this is on reduced external input lists; by the projection-pullback normal form of that node, the coherence of a general block is the pullback of the reduced one along the coordinate projection, so the lifted reduced data and the $\theta_r$ determine the full system.
